From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify hosted pricing: Chat vs Responses endpoints + discount eligibility

Hi Elena — great question. I put together a short breakdown below and attached our latest rate card. High-level summary first:

- Chat Completions: metered per token (input + output). Unit = 1 token; billed at hosted chat token rate from the rate card.
- Responses (new unified endpoint): metered at the same per-token economics once migrated, but we expose "response units" for easier forecasting. One response unit ≈ cost of 500 tokens; we show concrete mappings below.
- Legacy endpoints (Responses v0 / older chat endpoints): we'll continue to support them with a transitional mapping; usage will be converted to the equivalent token units on invoices.

Examples (approx):
- Short QA: 40 input tokens + 150 output tokens => 190 tokens => billed as 190 tokens under Chat; under Responses this is ~0.38 response units.
- Multi-turn conversation with KV cache: first turn pays full token count; repeated turns may be cheaper with prefix caching (savings depend on cache hit rate, we'll model if you share traces).

Discounts/packaging:
- Standard hosted baseline rates are in the attached redwood-ratecard-v3.pdf.
- Standard commit tiers: 10% off at $50k ARR, 15% at $150k, 20% at $300k (these are starting points; enterprise carve-outs possible).
- If Nimbus can commit to a 12-month minimum with predictable cadence, we can offer an accelerated discount schedule (up to additional 5% for >$250k ARR).

I can also produce a one-page mapping table using your CSV sample; looping in Rishi to confirm discounting authority.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — thanks for the patience. Per internal approvals, here's a clean summary for procurement and engineering:

1) Billing mapping (simplified):
- Chat Completions: billed per token (input+output) at hosted chat token rate (see rate card).
- Responses (new): billed using response units for forecast simplicity; invoices will convert response units to token cost using the same per-token rate. Net effect: same dollar-per-token once converted.
- Legacy endpoints: usage migrated to token-equivalent units on invoices during the transition window.

2) Concrete example (for PO modeling):
- 1 short QA (40 in + 150 out) = 190 tokens => invoice line ≈ 190 tokens
- 10k responses/week at average 200 tokens => ~2M tokens/month; use that to estimate monthly cost from the rate card.

3) Commercial offer (final):
- 12-month term, $150k ARR minimum guaranteed => 12% off published hosted rates.
- Accelerator: if total ARR >= $250k within the 12-mo term, a one-time retroactive credit that brings total discount to 17%.
- Standard terms apply otherwise (SLA, data controls as per our enterprise attachments).

I've attached the proposed quote and a one-page conversion appendix. If that looks good, sign via DocuSign and Procurement can issue a PO. HubSpot deal id: NR-202705.
